**Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 47, verses 4–9:**

**Explanation of the words:**

*"So when you meet those who disbelieve"*: That is, if the matter is as has been mentioned, then when you meet those who disbelieve on the battlefield, strike their necks with a severe blow by which you separate the heads from the bodies.

*"Until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them"*: That is, you have caused great killing among them, and they no longer have any hope of defeating you.

*"Then bind them firmly"*: That is, take them captive instead of killing them. *Wathaq* (bonds) means whatever a captive is bound with, whether leather or rope, so that they cannot escape and flee.

*"Then either release them as a favour or ransom them"*: That is, after you have taken them captive and bound them, you may either free them from captivity without compensation, or ransom them for property or for a Muslim prisoner. This is after the end of the battle.

*"Until the war lays down its burdens"*: That is, continue the fighting, the taking of captives and the capture until the war lays down its burdens, meaning its weapons. This happens when the disbelievers embrace Islam or enter your covenant. This is the final limit of the war, so that there is no more fitnah (strife) and religion is entirely for Allah.

*"That"*: That is, the matter is as you have learned: continued fighting until the disbelievers embrace Islam or enter your covenant and protection.

*"Had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them"*: That is, without any fighting by you, such as by causing the earth to swallow them or striking them with plague or the like.

*"But [He wills] to test some of you by means of others"*: But He commanded you to fight and prescribed it for you for a wisdom: that He may test some of you by others. That is, He tests which of you fight and which do not. The believer who is killed enters Paradise, and the disbeliever who is killed enters the Fire.

*"And those who are killed in the cause of Allah"*: That is, those killed by the enemy. It is also recited as *qatalu* (they fought) in the cause of Allah. [In this variant reading, the word is *qātalū*, while the common reading is *qutilū*.]

*"He will not let their deeds be lost"*: That is, He will not nullify or annul them.

*"He will guide them and improve their condition"*: That is, He will grant them success in what is good for them and their happiness, and will set their affairs right.

*"And admit them to Paradise, which He has made known to them"*: That is, on the Day of Resurrection He will admit them to Paradise, which He has described to them, so they will recognise it through the description He gave them in His Book and through the tongue of His Messenger (ﷺ).

*"If you support Allah"*: That is, in His religion, His Messenger and His believing servants.

*"He will support you and make your feet firm"*: That is, against your enemy, and He will make your feet firm in battles.

*"But those who disbelieve, for them is destruction"*: That is, may they perish, a perishing and a disappointment for them.

*"And He will make their deeds go astray"*: That is, He will nullify and annul them, so they gain nothing from them.

*"That"*: That is, the misguidance and the destruction.

*"Because they disliked what Allah has sent down"*: That is, the Qur'an, which contains various kinds of guidance and reform.

*"So He has rendered their deeds worthless"*: That is, He has nullified and annulled them, so they gain no benefit from them, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter.

**Meaning of the verses:**

It has already been established that those who disbelieved and barred others from the way of Allah, their deeds have been made to go astray because of their disbelief and their barring of others from the way of Allah. If the matter is so, then they must be fought to end both corruptions: their disbelief and their barring others from Islam. This is what the words of Allah the Exalted indicate: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, [strike] their necks﴾, meaning strike their necks with a blow that separates the head from the body, and continue fighting them ﴿until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, bind them firmly﴾, meaning tighten the binding of the captives by placing bonds, which are ropes, on their hands and feet, so that they cannot kill you or flee from you. After that, it is up to you and what your leader (imam) sees as the highest interest. If he sees fit to release them, then release them as a favour without compensation, or ransom them for property or for men. This will remain your condition: killing, taking captives and capture, then either free release as a favour or ransom in exchange for compensation, ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾, meaning its loads of equipment and military supplies. This happens when you reach the goal of war, which is that the disbeliever embraces Islam or enters the protection (dhimmah) of the Muslims. This is the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted in Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is for Allah﴾ [2:193]. As for His words ﴿That﴾, it means the matter you have learned: continued killing and capture until the war lays down its burdens, through entry into Islam or into the protection of the Muslims. His words ﴿Had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them﴾ mean without fighting by you, but by sinking into the earth, or plague, or thunderbolts from the sky. However, He did not do so, so that ﴿He may test some of you by means of others﴾, meaning to test you through them. He will know those of you who strive and endure, and He will test them through you, punishing whom He wills among them by your hands, and turning in mercy to whom He wills among them likewise. Your victory over them and their coming under your authority helps them to repent to Allah and return to the truth, so they submit and succeed in being saved from the Fire and entering Paradise. His words ﴿And those who were fought in the cause of Allah﴾ [or, in another reading, those who were killed in the cause of Allah]. This is general, covering the martyrs of Uhud and others, even though the verse was revealed about them. Allah the Exalted tells of His favour to them in His words: ﴿He will not let their deeds be lost﴾. ﴿He will guide them﴾ in this world, granting them success in every good, ﴿and improve their condition﴾. ﴿And He will admit them to Paradise﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿which He has made known to them﴾, meaning He has made it clear to them in His Book and through the tongue of His Messenger, and has also made it good for them. In the Hereafter He will guide them to their dwellings in Paradise, as the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of them is more guided to his dwelling in Paradise than to his dwelling that he had in this world." [Al-Bukhari].

His words ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and make your feet firm﴾: that is, O you who have believed in Allah as Lord, in Islam as religion, and in Muhammad as Messenger, if you support Allah by supporting His religion, His Prophet and His allies, by fighting His enemies, Allah will support you and grant you victory, and will make your feet firm in every battle in which you meet the polytheists and disbelievers. This is a promise from Allah the Exalted which He has fulfilled for His believing servants throughout the history of jihad in the cause of Allah. His words ﴿But those who disbelieve, for them is destruction﴾: that is, may they perish, and be destroyed, and lose and be ruined, ﴿and He will make their deeds go astray﴾, so they will not find them and will see no benefit from them whatsoever. This is the recompense and that is the punishment, ﴿because they disliked what Allah has sent down﴾, meaning the Qur'an with its verses of monotheism, laws and rulings, ﴿so He has rendered their deeds worthless﴾, meaning therefore He has rendered their deeds worthless, so they lost in both lives.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of these verses:

1. The obligation of jihad upon the Muslim community and its continuation, as Allah the Exalted explains in these verses, until no disbelieving combatant remains, either by their entering Islam or by their entering into a covenant and the protection of the Muslims and turning to reform themselves and prepare themselves for good and success.

2. The leader of the Muslims has the choice regarding captives between a free release and ransom, and also execution, based on evidence from the Sunnah.

3. Good news for those who strive in the cause of Allah of Allah's honouring and favouring them in this world and the Hereafter.

4. Whoever supports Allah's religion and His allies attains true victory.

5. A warning to the disbelievers of wretchedness and misery in this world and the Hereafter.

If the matter is so, then they must be fought to end both corruptions: their disbelief and their barring others from Islam. This is what the words of Allah the Exalted indicate: ﴿So when you meet those who disbelieve, [strike] their necks﴾, meaning strike their necks with a blow that separates the head from the body, and continue fighting them ﴿until, when you have inflicted slaughter upon them, bind them firmly﴾, meaning tighten the binding of the captives by placing bonds, which are ropes, on their hands and feet, so that they cannot kill you or flee from you. After that, it is up to you and what your leader (imam) sees as the highest interest. If he sees fit to release them, then release them as a favour without compensation, or ransom them for property or for men. This will remain your condition: killing, taking captives and capture, then either free release as a favour or ransom in exchange for compensation, ﴿until the war lays down its burdens﴾, meaning its loads of equipment and military supplies. This happens when you reach the goal of war, which is that the disbeliever embraces Islam or enters the protection (dhimmah) of the Muslims. This is the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted in Surah al-Baqarah: ﴿And fight them until there is no fitnah and religion is for Allah﴾ [2:193]. As for His words ﴿That﴾, it means the matter you have learned: continued killing and capture until the war lays down its burdens, through entry into Islam or into the protection of the Muslims. His words ﴿Had Allah willed, He would have taken vengeance upon them﴾ mean without fighting by you, but by sinking into the earth, or plague, or thunderbolts from the sky. However, He did not do so, so that ﴿He may test some of you by means of others﴾, meaning to test you through them. He will know those of you who strive and endure, and He will test them through you, punishing whom He wills among them by your hands, and turning in mercy to whom He wills among them likewise. Your victory over them and their coming under your authority helps them to repent to Allah and return to the truth, so they submit and succeed in being saved from the Fire and entering Paradise. His words ﴿And those who were fought in the cause of Allah﴾ [or, in another reading, those who were killed in the cause of Allah]. This is general, covering the martyrs of Uhud and others, even though the verse was revealed about them. Allah the Exalted tells of His favour to them in His words: ﴿He will not let their deeds be lost﴾. ﴿He will guide them﴾ in this world, granting them success in every good, ﴿and improve their condition﴾. ﴿And He will admit them to Paradise﴾ in the Hereafter, ﴿which He has made known to them﴾, meaning He has made it clear to them in His Book and through the tongue of His Messenger, and has also made it good for them. In the Hereafter He will guide them to their dwellings in Paradise, as the Messenger (ﷺ) said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, one of them is more guided to his dwelling in Paradise than to his dwelling that he had in this world." [Al-Bukhari].

His words ﴿O you who have believed, if you support Allah, He will support you and make your feet firm﴾: that is, O you who have believed in Allah as Lord, in Islam as religion, and in Muhammad as Messenger, if you support Allah by supporting His religion, His Prophet and His allies, by fighting His enemies, Allah will support you and grant you victory, and will make your feet firm in every battle in which you meet the polytheists and disbelievers. This is a promise from Allah the Exalted which He has fulfilled for His believing servants throughout the history of jihad in the cause of Allah. This is the recompense and that is the punishment, ﴿because they disliked what Allah has sent down﴾, meaning the Qur'an with its verses of monotheism, laws and rulings, ﴿so He has rendered their deeds worthless﴾, meaning therefore He has rendered their deeds worthless, so they lost in both lives.

**Guidance of the verses:**

From the guidance of these verses:

1. The obligation of jihad upon the Muslim community and its continuation, as Allah the Exalted explains in these verses, until no disbelieving combatant remains, either by their entering Islam or by their entering into a covenant and the protection of the Muslims and turning to reform themselves and prepare themselves for good and success.

2. The leader of the Muslims has the choice regarding captives between a free release and ransom, and also execution, based on evidence from the Sunnah.

3. Good news for those who strive in the cause of Allah of Allah's honouring and favouring them in this world and the Hereafter.

4. Whoever supports Allah's religion and His allies attains true victory.

5. A warning to the disbelievers of wretchedness and misery in this world and the Hereafter.

"Dammara Allahu 'alayhim wa-lil-kafirina amthaluha" (Allah destroyed them, and for the disbelievers there are similar [fates]): That is, Allah destroyed their dwellings upon them, so He destroyed them, their children and their wealth, and for the disbelievers there are the likes of that evil end.

"Wa-anna al-kafirina la mawla lahum" (And that the disbelievers have no protector): That is, they have no helper.

"Wa-alladhina kafaru yatamatta'una wa-ya'kuluna" (As for those who disbelieve, they enjoy themselves and eat): That is, they enjoy the worldly pleasures of food, drink and clothing, and they eat.

"Wa-ka'ayyin min qaryatin hiya ashaddu quwwatan" (And how many a town was stronger in might): That is, and many people of a town which was stronger in might.

"Min qaryatika allati akhrajatka" (than your town which has expelled you): That is, Makkah, when its people expelled the Prophet (ﷺ).

"Afaman kana 'ala bayyinatin min rabbihi" (Is one who stands upon clear proof from his Lord): That is, upon proof and evidence concerning the matter of his religion, so he worships Allah with knowledge.

"Kaman zuyyina lahu su'u 'amalihi" (like one for whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive): That is, like one for whom Satan has made the evil of his deeds attractive.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah the Exalted rebukes the polytheists who persist in shirk and disbelief, for their insistence on shirk and their obstinacy, saying: have they neglected? His saying "wa-lil-kafirina" [and for the disbelievers] there are the likes of that destructive end: a threat to the disbelievers of Makkah that a punishment like the punishment of the earlier peoples will descend upon them if they do not repent of their shirk, their persistence in it, and their obstinacy in it. His saying "dhalika" [that] – meaning the victory of the believers and the subduing of the disbelievers – is due to the fact that Allah is the Protector (mawla) of those who believe, that is, their Guardian, the one who manages their affairs and their helper, and that the disbelievers have no protector, because Allah forsakes them, and whoever Allah forsakes has no helper. His saying the Exalted: "Inna Allaha yudkhilu alladhina amanu wa-'amilu al-salihati jannatin tajri min tahtiha al-anhar" [Indeed, Allah will admit those who believe and do righteous deeds into gardens beneath which rivers flow]: this is a promise from Allah the Exalted to the people of faith and righteous deeds that He will admit them on the Day of Resurrection into gardens, that is, orchards, beneath whose palaces and trees rivers flow. His saying "wa-alladhina kafaru yatamatta'una" [and those who disbelieve enjoy themselves] in the world with its pleasures and desires, "wa-ya'kuluna kama ta'kulu al-an'am" [and eat as cattle eat], since they have no concern except their bellies and their private parts, and therefore they pay no attention to the Hereafter. "Wa-al-naru mathwan lahum" [and the Fire is their abode]: that is, a station, a dwelling and a final destination. This is a severe threat to the disbelievers, and this is the method of encouragement and warning that is a prominent characteristic of the Qur'an's style in guiding mankind. The meaning of the noble verse: many of the towns whose people were stronger in might than the people of your town, Makkah, which expelled you, since they had decided to execute him (ﷺ), We destroyed – that is, the people of those towns – and there was no helper found for them when We destroyed them. So this verse carries consolation for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and what a consolation!! His saying the Exalted: "Afaman kana 'ala bayyinatin min rabbihi" [Is one who stands upon clear proof from his Lord], that is, upon knowledge and evidence of the soundness of his belief and his worship of Allah the Exalted, hoping for His reward and fearing His punishment – and these are the believers – "kaman zuyyina lahu su'u 'amalihi" [like one for whom the evil of his deeds has been made attractive], that is, his ugly deeds of shirk and disbelief, so he worships idols, "wa-ittaba'u ahwa'ahum" [and follow their desires], they in that do not follow any divine revelation or human reason. So is their state like the state of those mentioned before them? The answer: they are not alike, for between them are differences like the difference between life and death, and Paradise and Fire.

3- Explaining the difference between the materialists and the people of faith and steadfastness upon the method of Islam.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 47, verse 15:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Min ma'in ghayri asin﴾ (of water not turned putrid): that is, its smell and taste have not changed due to long standing.

﴿Wa anharun min 'asalin musaffan﴾ (and rivers of clarified honey): that is, from wax and the excretions of bees.

﴿Wa suqu ma'an hamiman﴾ (and they will be given boiling water to drink): that is, water that is extremely hot.

﴿Fa qatta'a am'a'ahum﴾ (so that it cuts their bowels to pieces): that is, their intestines, so that they come out from their posteriors.

Meaning of the verses:

His Exalted saying, ﴿The description of the Garden promised to the God-fearing﴾: this noble verse contains a full explanation of the rivers of Paradise and the drink of the people of the Fire. It also includes a comparison between the state of the people of faith and piety, and what they were promised of forgiveness of their sins and entry into Paradise, and the state of the people of the Fire, who abide therein forever and who were promised therein various kinds of severe punishment. So His saying ﴿The description of the Garden﴾ means its attribute, which represents it and explains its state, which was promised to the God-fearing, that is, which Allah the Exalted promised to His servants who are mindful of Him, namely His friends who worshipped Him and affirmed His oneness, obeying Him in His commands and prohibitions, and by that guarding themselves against shirk and sins. ﴿Therein are rivers of water not turned putrid﴾, that is, whose taste and smell have not changed due to long standing; and rivers of milk whose taste has not changed, that is, it has not turned sour and has not become sharp, and therefore its smell has not changed either; and rivers of wine, a delight for those who drink it, that is, therein are rivers of wine which are a delight to whoever drinks it, and the reason for its delightfulness is that it is neither turbid, nor intoxicating, nor does it have any unpleasant smell; and rivers of clarified honey, that is, therein are rivers of clarified honey, that is, from wax and the excretions of bees. Guidance from the verses:

1- Piety is the cause that brings about Paradise; so Allah the Mighty and Majestic has made it. Piety, after faith, is performing what is commanded and abandoning what is forbidden, of all kinds of shirk and sins.

2- Explanation of some of the bounties of Paradise, including drinks and fruits.

3- Explanation of some of the punishment of the Fire, which is abiding therein forever and drinking boiling water.

4- Affirmation of the Resurrection and recompense, and that there is no equality between the people of happiness and the people of misery.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 47, verses 16–19:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And among them are those who listen to you﴾: That is, among the disbelieving hypocrites are those who listen to you during the Friday sermon.

﴿What did he just say?﴾: That is, "just now" (ā'nifan). They say this in mockery and derision, meaning that it is something not worth heeding or taking into account, because of its lack of benefit.

﴿Allah has sealed their hearts﴾: That is, with disbelief, so they do not comprehend.

﴿And followed their desires﴾: That is, in disbelief and hypocrisy.

﴿And those who were guided﴾: That is, the believers.

﴿He increased them in guidance﴾: That is, Allah increased them in guidance.

﴿And gave them their piety﴾: That is, He inspired them with what they use to protect themselves from the punishment of Allah, the Exalted.

﴿Do they await anything but the Hour﴾: That is, the people of Makkah await nothing but the Hour.

﴿That it will come upon them suddenly﴾: That is, unexpectedly.

﴿Its signs have already come﴾: That is, its signs (ashrāt, sing. ashrāt is the plural of shart, "sign"), such as the sending of the Prophet ﷺ, the splitting of the moon, and the smoke.

﴿How, then, when it has come to them, will their reminder be of use?﴾: That is, how will they benefit from remembrance when it comes to them, since the door of repentance has already been closed?

﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah﴾: That is, based on what has preceded, O our Prophet, know that none deserves worship except Allah, so worship Him and rely upon Him.

﴿And ask forgiveness for your sin﴾: That is, say, "I ask Allah's forgiveness," or "O Allah, forgive me."

﴿And for the believing men and believing women﴾: That is, and seek forgiveness for the believing men and believing women.

﴿And Allah knows your activity [by day] and your resting place [by night]﴾: That is, your movement during the day as you conduct the affairs of your worldly life, and your resting place (mathwākum), meaning the place of your stay and your sleep at night.

Explanation of the verses:

The words of the Most High, "And among them are those who listen to you" [16], and the verse after it, are without doubt Medinan, because they were revealed concerning the hypocrites. The Most High informs His Messenger about some of the hypocrites: ﴿And among them﴾, that is, among some of the hypocrites, ﴿are those who listen to you﴾, that is, to your speech on Friday while you address the people from the pulpit. ﴿Until, when they leave from your presence﴾, that is, from the mosque, ﴿they say to those who were given knowledge﴾ among your companions, such as Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, ﴿"What did he just say?"﴾. Their statement is clearly evidence of their corruption, since if they were believers who loved [the Messenger] they would have said, "What did the Messenger of Allah just say?" But they said, "What did he just say?", meaning that what the Messenger ﷺ said is not something beneficial worth heeding. The Most High said: ﴿Those﴾, that is, the far-gone in evil and hypocrisy, ﴿are those upon whose hearts Allah has sealed﴾, that is, with disbelief and hypocrisy, because of their great defilement with the filth of disbelief and hypocrisy, until that covered their hearts, so it became a seal and stamp upon them. ﴿And followed their desires﴾: these are two causes. The first is the sealing, which prevents the seeking of guidance; the second is following desire, which blinds and deafens. Therefore they do not become guided. The Most High's words, ﴿And those who were guided﴾, to sound faith and righteous deeds, ﴿Allah increased them in guidance﴾, according to His custom regarding the growth, purification and increase of things, ﴿and gave them their piety﴾, that is, inspired them with what they should guard against and helped them to do so, so they guard against what displeases Allah, the Exalted, the greatest of which is shirk and sins. The Most High's words in the third verse of this context [18], ﴿Do they await anything﴾, that is, the disbelieving Quraysh, the leaders of disbelief in Makkah, ﴿but the Hour﴾, that is, they await nothing but the Hour, meaning the Resurrection, ﴿that it will come upon them suddenly﴾, that is, unexpectedly. If they do not look to the Hour with their faith, then the Hour's signs have already come. The first of its signs is the sending of Muhammad ﷺ, the second is the smoke, and the third is the splitting of the moon.

The Most High's words, ﴿How, then, when it has come to them, will their reminder be of use?﴾: that is, how will they have a remembrance that benefits them when the Hour comes, or rather when its conditions, meaning the appearance of its major signs, come? Repentance will not be accepted from anyone who was not a believer, as the Most High said in Surah al-An'am: ﴿On the day when some of the signs of your Lord come, a soul will not benefit from its faith if it had not believed before, or had not earned good through its faith﴾ [Verse: 158]. In any case, the verse rebukes the disbelievers of Makkah for delaying their faith, which has no reason, given the clarity of the proofs of reason and transmission and the evident arguments and evidences indicating the oneness of Allah and the obligation to worship Him alone, to the exclusion of anything else. Therefore the Most High said: ﴿So know that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sin and for the believing men and believing women﴾, that is, know, O Muhammad, that there is no one worthy of worship and fit for it except Allah, who is the Creator and Owner of everything, and ask your Lord for forgiveness for yourself and for the believing men and believing women. Although this address is directed to the Messenger ﷺ, what is truly intended, or primarily intended, is others besides him ﷺ. It is as if the Most High said: O servants of Allah, O people, with the Messenger at your head: know that there is no deity except Allah, and ask forgiveness for your sins, as believing men and believing women. ﴿And Allah knows your activity﴾, that is, your movement during the day in the interests of your livelihood and your afterlife, ﴿and knows your resting place﴾ in your beds while you sleep. He knows you in whatever state you are in at every hour of night or day, so fear Him and be mindful of Him, until you succeed in His pleasure in the Gardens of Bliss.

Lessons from the verses:

1- It is permissible for a surah to be Meccan while containing one or more Medinan verses.

2- A warning against following desire, for it blinds and deafens, and we seek refuge in Allah.

3- Clarification that the Hour has signs (ashrāt), meaning indications that appear before it and thus point to its nearness.

4- The obligation to know that there is no deity except Allah, which is achieved by the following method:

Acknowledging that a human being is created like the other creatures around him, and every creature must have a creator. Who then created the human being and the universe? The answer, certainly, is Allah. Since Allah is the Creator, whatever is other than Him is a created thing dependent upon Allah, its Creator, for the preservation of its life. Who, then, is worshipped and served: the Creator or the created? The answer: the Creator. Thus it is established that there is no object of worship except Allah, and this is the meaning of "there is no deity except Allah." And since worship is known only through revelation, belief in the Messenger of Allah is obligatory, so it became necessary to add "Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah." Thus we say: "There is no deity except Allah, Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah."

"Fa-idha 'azam al-amr" (But when the matter is resolved upon): i.e., when fighting is made obligatory and the command to go out to it is established.

"Fa-law sadaqu Allah" (If they had been true to Allah): i.e., by Allah, if they had fulfilled what they pledged, that they would fight.

"La-kana khayran lahum" (It would have been better for them): i.e., fulfilling what they pledged would have been better for them in their worldly life and their hereafter.

"Fa-hal 'asaytum in tawallaytum" (Would you then, if you turned away): i.e., if you turned away from the nominal faith you are upon and declared your disbelief.

"An tufsidu fi al-ardi wa tuqatti'u arhamakum" (that you would cause corruption on earth and sever your ties of kinship): i.e., you would cause corruption on earth through shirk and sins, and not maintain your ties of kinship.

"Fa-asamahum wa a'ma absarahum" (So He deafened them and blinded their eyes): i.e., Allah, exalted is He, did this to them, so they do not hear the truth and do not see good and right guidance.

Explanation of the verses:

The words "Wa yaqulu alladhina amanu" (And those who believe say) through the end of the surah: the apparent sense is that it is Medinan, not Meccan, and so it is; the majority of the verses of this surah are Medinan. And there is no difficulty, because fighting was not enjoined until after the Prophetic migration, and hypocrisy likewise did not appear until after the migration, and the context now is the treatment of hypocrisy and the matters of jihad. Allah, exalted is He, says: "And those who believe say, from among the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, desiring jihad: 'Why has a surah not been sent down?'" That is, why did Allah not send down a Qur'anic surah commanding jihad? Allah, exalted is He, says: "But when a clear, definitive surah is sent down, in which there is no abrogation, and in which fighting is mentioned," that is, the command to it and encouragement toward it. As for His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who turned back on their heels﴾: That is: they reverted to disbelief in their hearts, not merely with their tongues, and they are the hypocrites. ﴿After guidance had become clear to them﴾: That is: the truthfulness of the Messenger ﷺ and the soundness of his religion, Islam. Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 47, verses 33–38:

Explanation of the words:

"And do not nullify your deeds": that is, by showing off (riya'), associating partners with God (shirk), and acts of disobedience.

"And they hindered [others] from the way of God": that is, from Islam.

"Then God will not forgive them": that is, because they died in disbelief, and disbelief nullifies deeds.

"So do not weaken and call to peace": that is, do not be feeble and call for reconciliation with the disbelievers.

"And you will have the upper hand": that is, you will be the victors, the dominant ones.

"And He will not deprive you of your deeds": that is, He will not diminish the reward of your deeds and their recompense.

"The life of this world is but amusement and diversion": that is, occupying oneself with this world and devoting oneself to it is nothing but diversion and play, because there is no benefit in it.

"And He does not ask you for your wealth": that is, He does not require you to spend all your wealth, but only the zakat.

"And if He should ask it of you and press you, you would be stingy": that is, by insisting excessively on your giving of wealth, you would become miserly.

"And He would bring forth your resentment": that is, your malice and hatred toward the religion of Islam.

"And whoever is stingy is only stingy toward himself": that is, its consequence falls on himself and not on others; it is he who deprives himself of the reward.

"And if you turn away, He will replace you with another people": that is, if you turn away from obedience to God and His Messenger, He will bring others in your place.

"Then they will not be like you": that is, in obedience; they will be more obedient to God and His Messenger than you.

Explanation of the verses:

When God mentioned the disbelievers and their opposition to His Messenger ﷺ, He addressed the believers and commanded them to obey Him and His Messenger, saying: "O you who have believed, obey God and obey the Messenger," meaning in what they command you and forbid you, of beliefs, statements and deeds. "And do not nullify your deeds," meaning He forbids them from nullifying their deeds through shirk, riya' and acts of disobedience; the intended meaning of nullifying deeds is depriving them of their reward. Then He informed them, admonishing and advising them, saying: "Indeed, those who disbelieve," in God and His Messenger, "and hinder [others] from the way of God," meaning from Islam, by whatever means, "and then die while they are disbelievers before repenting. These, God will not forgive them, and He will punish them with the punishment prepared for their likes." Then He informed them, admonishing and advising them, saying: "Indeed, those who disbelieve," in God and His Messenger, "and hinder [others] from the way of God," meaning from Islam, by whatever means, "and then die while they are disbelievers before repenting. These, God will not forgive them, and He will punish them with the punishment prepared for their likes." And His saying, exalted is He: "So do not weaken and call to peace while you have the upper hand, and God is with you, and He will not deprive you of your deeds," God forbids His believing servants from being feeble in fighting their enemies among the disbelievers, and from calling the disbelievers to reconciliation and truce while they are strong and capable. This is the meaning of His saying "while you have the upper hand," meaning the victors, the dominant. "And He will not deprive you of your deeds," meaning He will not diminish the reward of your deeds; rather He will recompense you for them and increase you from His bounty. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, the life of this world is but amusement and diversion﴾. This is a fact: if the servant turns to this world, forgetful of the Hereafter and devoted to the world, it will be for him nothing but diversion and play, in that he has gained no true profit from it and it has brought him no good or happiness. It is like the player who amuses himself with something for a while, and then the play brings him nothing, like the play and diversion of children, for they play and divert themselves earnestly, then they return to their parents asking for food and drink. And His saying: "And if you believe," meaning true belief, "and fear God," meaning avoid what angers and displeases your Lord from shirk and acts of disobedience, "He will give you your rewards, which are consequent upon belief and piety."

And His saying: "And He does not ask you for your wealth," meaning He does not demand all your wealth, since He dislikes that He should ask it of you and press you so that you become stingy, for it is well known of human nature that when a person is pressed and insisted upon for money, he becomes stingy and does not give, and may even abandon Islam for that reason. And His saying: "And He would bring forth your resentment," meaning your malice and hatred toward the religion and your dislike of it; this is why He does not ask your wealth of you. And His exalted saying: ﴿Here you are, those invited to spend in the way of God﴾, meaning a portion of your wealth in zakat or jihad, not all your wealth, since He knows the soul's stinginess with wealth. And His saying: ﴿And among you is one who is stingy﴾, meaning withholds; and whoever is stingy is only stingy toward himself, for it is he who deprives himself of the reward of spending in the way of God, which carries great reward. And His saying: ﴿And God is the Rich, and you are the poor﴾ toward God, exalted is He. He is free of need from you and does not urge you to spend because He needs it, but because you need it, for through it your souls are purified, your affairs are set in order, and you are victorious over your enemy. And His saying: "And if you turn away," meaning you return from Islam to disbelief, God forbid, "He will replace you with another people," meaning He will remove you and bring others, "then they will not be like you," but they will be more obedient to God, exalted is He, and quicker to carry out what is asked of them. Far be it from them to turn away, and they did not turn away, nor did God replace them with others. This is only from the category of urging them toward lofty matters and holding fast to their resolute duties, in view of their station in this nation: they are its most noble, most complete, most obedient to God, and most beloved to Him and to His Messenger ﷺ.

Guidance from the verses:

1- The obligation to obey God and obey His Messenger.

2- The obligation to complete a righteous deed, such as prayer and others, once one has begun it.

3- The nullification of a righteous deed by showing off, by spoiling it while performing it, or by apostasy from Islam.

4- The prohibition of inclining toward reconciliation with enemies while one is able to fight them and capable of repelling their harm.

5- Discouragement from being absorbed in this world and turning away from the Hereafter.

6- The prohibition of stinginess when one has wealth and abundance.
